text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $135.46, continuing a sharp six-day decline that has wiped out 10% of the stock's value since late October. The immediate trigger was the company's quarterly earnings announcement on November 5th; without seeing the actual results, the timing and scale of the selloff suggest investor disappointment with profitability or forward guidance, though oil prices themselves remain relatively stable (US crude at $99.64/barrel). The broader context matters too: oil majors face new political headwinds after the midterm elections, with incoming Democratic scrutiny of energy deals and policies that could constrain operations and returns.

The stock's losses also reflect deeper uncertainty in the energy sector. While some executives are betting on a "demand decade" ahead for oil and gas, the commentary emphasizes geopolitical risks and price volatility—and ConocoPhillips, as a U.S. independent with global operations, sits at the crossroads of all three (political risk, commodity exposure, and operational complexity).
